clause_by_clause_review.producer_reason_reviewed: Treasury implementation authority for Resolution 778 and repaid assets is prospective authority revoked expressly by EO13350; no factual completion date is inferred from a transfer program.

The financial-institution transfer command is conditional on Treasury determinations and directions and is revoked prospectively by EO13350. Receipt of one transfer would not prove every potential transfer completed.
New York Federal Reserve receipt, holding, investment and onward transfers are continuing commands until revoked, with accrued obligations addressed as residuals.

Discharge, good-faith protection and preservation of pre-transfer rights are assessed expressly: protection for transactions already performed can remain accrued, but it supplies no independent command to make new transfers after revocation.
The financial-institution definition serves the transfer/implementation commands and has no independent prospective operation after those commands are revoked.
Treasury rulemaking, redelegation and all-agency implementation duties implement this order and are expressly revoked with it; preserved prior actions and matured duties are residual matters.
The no-private-right clause limits enforcement of this order and is ancillary to the order's implementation; it does not supply an independent ongoing asset-transfer mandate.

Immediate effectiveness and transmittal/publication concern enactment and notice of this order; completed notice is not a current independent obligation. The last prospective authority is expressly revoked effective July 30, 2004, 12:01 a.m. EDT under EO13350 section 10.

inventory_review.scope_note: EO12734 and EO12817 retain full text but merge notice commands with differently timed legal acts; EO12722 needs the stated declaration/definition/notice splits; EO12696 selected text is truncated.

limits: This is AI source review, not an eo-lifecycle-review/v1 independent_human record.
Prospective-authority cessation can be supported while the exact submitted complete first-end claim is rejected.
Original page-image confirmation is not asserted; three EO13350 legal-body rendered pages were independently inspected.
rationale: The overrides restore sections 1 and 2 omitted/conflated by machine segmentation and include all eight numbered sections. Sections 1-3 separately concern Treasury implementation, conditional financial-institution transfers and Federal Reserve receipt/holding/investment/transfers. Sections 4-7 address discharge/good-faith and pre-transfer rights, definition, implementation/redelegation/all-agency commands and enforcement limitation. The express revocation and July 30, 2004 effectiveness support cessation of prospective authority; EO13350 continuing blocking names EO12722/12724, not new EO12817 transfers. Accrued section 4 protections may persist without creating new transfer commands. This substantive cessation conclusion does not cure the exact first-end defect for section 8.

required_corrections_or_open_tasks.reason: The corrected inventory merges section 8(a) immediate effectiveness and section 8(b) congressional transmittal/publication and assigns the complete scope first_end July 30, 2004. The original is published in the Federal Register October 23, 1992, so that publication command did not first cease in 2004. “Completed notice is not a current independent obligation” does not prove a 2004 exact first-end field. Actual congressional transmittal completion is unheld.
required_corrections_or_open_tasks.required_correction: Separate section 8(a), section 8(b) publication, and congressional transmittal as needed to account for their distinct legal roles and first ends. Preserve the supported July 30, 2004 revocation of prospective sections 1-3/6 authorities. Provide exact notice-completion evidence, or withdraw approval for the complete claim and classify unable. Do not infer exhaustion of all assets, UN repayments, Treasury determinations or transmittal from the revocation.
